full_text_en:
Vladimir Valerievich Volkov et al. — Robbery and Escape Case

Defendant: Vladimir Valerievich Volkov, male, 25 years old, Russian nationality. Arrested on March 8, 1993.

Defendant: Oleg Viktorovich Kriminok, male, 22 years old, Ukrainian nationality. Arrested on March 8, 1993.

Defense Counsel: Zhang Zhicheng, attorney at Beifang Law Firm, Harbin, Heilongjiang Province.

Defendant: Denis Valerievich Shevtsov, male, 22 years old, Ukrainian nationality. Arrested on March 8, 1993.

Defense Counsel: An Qingwen, attorney at Heilongjiang Meng Fanxu Law Firm.

Defendant: Mikhail Anatolyevich Moskalenko, male, 20 years old, Russian nationality. Arrested on March 8, 1993.

Defense Counsel: Meng Fanxu and Qin Yadong, attorneys at Heilongjiang Meng Fanxu Law Firm.

The above four defendants, Vladimir Valerievich Volkov et al., were prosecuted by the People's Procuratorate of Harbin, Heilongjiang Province, the People's Republic of China, before the Harbin Intermediate People's Court for robbery and escape. The Harbin Intermediate People's Court, with the participation of interpreters Xu Zhongxin, Lai Tianrong, Wang Songting, Ma Chunru, and others, conducted a public trial and found as follows:

On February 2, 1993, the defendants Vladimir Valerievich Volkov, Oleg Viktorovich Kriminok, Denis Valerievich Shevtsov, and Mikhail Anatolyevich Moskalenko entered the territory of China with a private tourist group through the Suifenhe port in Heilongjiang Province. On February 7, they arrived in Harbin and stayed in Room 324 of the Beiyuan Hotel. While exchanging US dollars for RMB illegally at the Chinese-Foreign Civilian Market in Harbin, Volkov became acquainted with the victims Qi Yuting (male, 22 years old) and Zhang Xiaocheng (male, 27 years old). The two victims, through Volkov, also came to know defendants Kriminok, Shevtsov, and Moskalenko. During the process of exchanging US dollars for RMB with the two victims, Volkov conceived the idea of robbery. He proposed the plan, and the other three defendants agreed. After premeditation, Kriminok purchased bandages and adhesive tape for the crime. To conceal their true identities, Volkov and Moskalenko, falsely claiming that their passports had been withheld, borrowed the passports of two foreign tourists staying in Harbin through Anatoly Eduardovich Viktorov, a Russian studying at Harbin Institute of Technology. They then rented Room 410 of the Beiyuan Hotel. At noon on February 24, 1993, Volkov instructed the other three defendants to gather in Room 410 and wait, while he went alone to the Chinese-Foreign Civilian Market, found Qi Yuting and Zhang Xiaocheng, and under the pretext of exchanging US dollars, lured the two victims to Room 410 of the Beiyuan Hotel. Upon entering, Volkov immediately strangled Qi Yuting with a pre-prepared rope and threatened him with a sharp knife; Shevtsov twisted Zhang Xiaocheng's hands behind his back; Moskalenko stood guard at the door. Then Kriminok tied Zhang Xiaocheng's hands and feet with a rope, gagged him with a bandage, and sealed his mouth with adhesive tape, stealing RMB 21,000 from the pocket of Zhang Xiaocheng's jacket. Shevtsov tied Qi Yuting's hands and feet, gagged him with a bandage, and sealed his mouth with adhesive tape; Moskalenko stole RMB 19,200 from Qi Yuting's person. Volkov threatened Qi Yuting with a knife not to report the crime. Thereafter, the four defendants fled by taxi to Daqing City, Heilongjiang Province. On February 26, the four defendants were apprehended by the public security authorities and detained in the detention center of the Heilongjiang Provincial Public Security Department. All stolen money was recovered and returned to the victims.

At approximately 1:00 a.m. on April 13, 1993, defendant Vladimir Valerievich Volkov pried open the iron bars on the window of the detention cell and escaped from the detention center. On April 19, 1993, Volkov was captured at Xingweicun Station in Nanjing, Jiangsu Province.

The above facts are confirmed by the victims Qi Yuting and Zhang Xiaocheng's identification of the four defendants and their testimony regarding the robbery, which is consistent with the confessions of the four defendants; the testimony of witness Anatoly Eduardovich Viktorov, confirming the process of borrowing passports for Volkov to rent Room 410 of the Beiyuan Hotel; physical evidence such as the confiscated knife, ropes, bandages, adhesive tape used in the crime, and the recovered stolen money of RMB 40,200; expert examination evidence that the fracture marks on the adhesive tape used to seal the victims' mouths matched those on the adhesive tape carried by the defendants when they fled the scene; the testimony of taxi driver Li Bo, confirming that he drove the four defendants to Daqing City; and the testimony of police officers from the Nanjing East Railway Station Police Station, confirming the capture of Volkov after his escape.

The Harbin Intermediate People's Court held: In accordance with Article 3 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that any person who commits a crime within the territory of the People's Republic of China shall be subject to the Criminal Law of the PRC, unless otherwise specially provided by law, the defendants, as foreign nationals, should have abided by Chinese laws and engaged in lawful tourism and commercial activities upon entering China. Instead, upon Volkov's proposal and organization, after careful preparation, they used violent means such as tying up, gagging, and threatening with a knife to rob the victims of a substantial amount of cash, seriously infringing upon the property rights and personal rights of Chinese citizens. Their conduct violated Article 150(1) of the Criminal Law and constituted the crime of robbery. The circumstances of the crime were serious and should be punished in accordance with Article 150(2) of the Criminal Law. The four defendants carried out the robbery with premeditation, which meets the requirements of Article 22 of the Criminal Law, and are joint intentional offenders. Volkov initiated the criminal intent and organized the execution of the crime; pursuant to Article 23 of the Criminal Law, he is the principal offender who played a major role in the joint crime and shall be given a heavier punishment. After his arrest, Volkov escaped from the detention center, and his conduct constituted the crime of escape under Article 161 of the Criminal Law. Volkov committed multiple crimes; according to Article 64 of the Criminal Law, the punishment for the crime of escape shall be merged with that for the crime of robbery. Defendants Kriminok and Shevtsov, during the robbery, tied the victims' hands and feet, and used bandages and adhesive tape to gag and seal the victims' mouths, actively participating in the crime. However, the roles they played were secondary compared to the principal offender. Pursuant to Article 24 of the Criminal Law, they are accomplices and shall be given a lighter punishment than the principal offender. Defendant Moskalenko stood guard for his accomplices during the robbery and, after the accomplices had tied up the victims, took money from the victims' persons. He is an accomplice who played a subsidiary role in the joint crime and, pursuant to Article 24 of the Criminal Law, shall be given a mitigated punishment compared to the principal offender. The tools used by the defendants in the crime shall be confiscated in accordance with Article 60 of the Criminal Law. Accordingly, on March 22, 1994, the Harbin Intermediate People's Court rendered the following judgment:

1. Defendant Vladimir Valerievich Volkov is convicted of the crime of robbery and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of fourteen years; he is convicted of the crime of escape and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of three years; the sentences are to be merged and the combined sentence is fixed-term imprisonment of sixteen years.

2. Defendant Oleg Viktorovich Kriminok is convicted of the crime of robbery and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of ten years.

3. Defendant Denis Valerievich Shevtsov is convicted of the crime of robbery and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of ten years.

4. Defendant Mikhail Anatolyevich Moskalenko is convicted of the crime of robbery and sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of five years.

5. The knife, ropes, gauze, and adhesive tape seized in this case, which were the tools used by the defendants in the commission of the crime, are to be confiscated.

After the judgment was pronounced, all four defendants appealed. Vladimir Valerievich Volkov appealed on the grounds that he was a first-time offender, had a good attitude in admitting his guilt, and that the sentence was too heavy. Oleg Viktorovich Kriminok appealed on the grounds that he was a first-time offender, did not cause physical injury to the victims, and that the stolen money was returned in full, and therefore a lighter sentence should be imposed. Denis Valerievich Shevtsov appealed on the grounds that he had truthfully confessed his crime and that the sentence was too heavy. Mikhail Anatolyevich Moskalenko appealed on the grounds that he had a good attitude in admitting his guilt and that the sentence was too heavy. They each appealed to the Heilongjiang High People's Court.

After trial, the Heilongjiang High People's Court held: The facts raised by the four appellants—that they were first-time offenders, did not cause physical injury to the victims, and had truthfully confessed their crimes—had already been considered in the first-instance judgment. The stolen money was recovered by the public security authorities after the defendants were captured and then returned to the victims; it was not returned in full by the defendants themselves. Therefore, the request for a lighter sentence on this basis is manifestly groundless and shall not be accepted. The first-instance judgment found the facts of the crimes of the four appellants clear, the evidence conclusive, the conviction accurate, the sentence appropriate, and the trial procedures lawful, and it should be affirmed. Accordingly, on May 13, 1994, the Heilongjiang High People's Court ruled: The appeals of Vladimir Valerievich Volkov and the other three appellants are dismissed, and the original judgment is affirmed.
